The Swift binary is a SKELETON (RULE #1): it ships a clamped tempo-heuristic fallback and reads THIS file at runtime for the real genre feel. Zero-rebuild to tune. Schema owner: LoopStarGenrePack.swift.
name: Reggae
blurb: Roots reggae one-drop: dubby air, a staccato offbeat organ skank, and a deep bass that leaves the one open and lands the pocket.

flavors.label: Roots One Drop
flavors.blurb: Classic seventies roots: rim and kick together on three, minor seesaw down to bVII, plenty of air left in the bar.

flavors.label: Rockers Drive
flavors.blurb: Sly-and-Robbie steppers push: kick on every beat, the dread descent turning over, no let-up in the skank.

flavors.label: Dub Tunnel
flavors.blurb: One minor chord for the whole ride, the way a dub plate sits still while the mix does the moving.

flavors.label: Lovers Rock
flavors.blurb: Sweet major-key soul reggae: a soft organ bubble, add6 colour on the tonic, a singer's tempo.

flavors.label: Early Ska Skank
flavors.blurb: Bright and quick, hard triad chops on every offbeat, all Skatalites shuffle and no dub.

arranger.llmStyleBrief: Reggae harmony is modal and static. Minor tunes lean i-bVII or dorian i-IV; major tunes sit on I with add6 or add9 colour. Chords change every two bars, often not at all - the riddim carries the tune, not the changes. Cadences are plagal iv-i or modal bVII-i. Never V7, never ii-V, never maj7.
